I've planned round 336 as **RETRO 336**, the retrospective covering rounds 321–335; the decision in `b-next.json` is **CONTINUE**. Because today (2026-11-04) is before 2026-11-05, the order fixed in the round-335 planning makes 336 the RETRO, with REGRESSION following. Nothing external blocks the loop.

**Round 335 is closed from evidence.** C passed it (11 rows, 0 bugs, `browserVerified` and `realVerified` true) and gate 335 published `f1def9c` to both remotes. Stage c3-i of PERF-DRAG-PREVIEW is marked done. `f1def9c` is the baseline for round 336; `context/head-sha.txt` was stale and still said `0d22ab9`, so I checked git directly. The old task is archived as `tasks/round-335.md`, byte-equal to the original.

**What the retro found:**
- **Results:** C passed 10 rounds and failed 5 (321, 322, 323, 327, 329). The gate published 9, skipped 5 and failed 1 (325). The window cost $339.76, and the last six rounds (330–335) all passed and were published.
- **Causes:** four of the five failures came from my own specs or sketches. Lessons already in the file cover three of them; the fourth (327, where A's reviewer flagged my sketch and C still ran) gets a new rule.
- **Screen:** nothing visible changed in 15 rounds, because they were all performance rounds. The visible text is identical to retro 321 at both viewports.
- **Experiment from retro 321 (EXP-R321-PRECHECK-GATES):** interim reading is "not evaluable as specified". I never ran more than 2 of the 6 named gate checks on my sketches. The final verdict is due at RETRO 351.

**What changed in `lessons.md`** (still 59 lines, all suggested by `tech-lead`):
- **L58:** I run the code-reviewer on my own sketch before dispatch. A row I could not run on the sketch is written as "record — not run on sketch: reason".
- **L22:** when A stops on a ruled clause and leaves a diff, C does a short round instead of a full one. This replaces raising the "send a STOP back to B" request to you a fifth time.
- **L57:** C starts recording the checks a change can actually affect, from round 337.

**One new systemic task, SYS-R336-PERF-DRAG-WINDOW.** It is test-only: one shared drag-window helper in the perf spec, closing six findings from rounds 335. I queued it before c3-ii; the gate reviewer preferred after, and that disagreement is recorded in the retro.

**Round 336 task:** A only confirms the tree is unchanged. C checks every retro number against its source and runs three browser rows at both viewports: the screen re-capture, the auth guard, and a Studio smoke that now includes the cross-lane move, Undo and a WAV export.

**For you (Saba):**
- `user-review/screen-review-336.md` has two new questions: SR-336-1, where the footer names one insert point but the stem was placed at another, and SR-336-2, a half-cut library row after scrolling.
- The weakest step of the buyer's journey is still SR-305-3: "Try it in the Studio" lands on an empty timeline.
- 88 questions are waiting for your answer; none blocks the loop.

**For root:**
- The backlog clean-up script moved R80-RECORDINGS-FIELD-BORDERS (Medium) into the archive. It is still open evidence that needs a check with the backend, so it should stay in the active list.
- Architecture checkpoint D-29z915 is still unanswered. Two architecture questions whose deadline was this retro are attached in `b-round-335.md` §8.
- The `backlog.json` text diff will look large because it is now written as plain UTF-8; the content changes are additions only.

**Consults:** `tech-lead` and `product-designer` were really consulted. The advisor was available and I used it twice; its second review led to sourcing every closure claim, confirming the C-cost drop matches a model change (Opus to Sonnet from round 332), and naming the smoke's target lane exactly. The other reviewers the retro policy names are not on this phase's consult list, and I didn't speak for them. The store is unchanged: clean tree, all 1,236 files match the frozen list, and `b-round-335/claims-336.sh` passes.
